Prostate-specific antigen monitoring
Measurement of PSA is the cornerstone of follow-up after local treatment. While PSA thresholds depend on the

interventions.body:
WHAT I FOUND
**radiology_report**: The mpMRI prostate exam showed a focal hypo-intense lesion in the left peripheral zone at the base, measuring approximately 18 mm in maximal diameter. Diffusion-weighted imaging showed marked restriction within this region, with corresponding low apparent diffusion coefficient values. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences revealed early and intense focal enhancement in the same area. The impression was PI-RADS 5 lesion in the left peripheral zone at the base, with a PSA density of 2.306 ng/mL/mL and a clinical T stage cT2.
**pathology_report**: Histological examination of the prostate tissue revealed adenocarcinoma with a Gleason score of 4+4, corresponding to ISUP grade group 4. The tumour was located at the base, left, and a cribriform pattern was present within the malignant glands. The AI-predicted ISUP grade group (digital pathology) was grade group 5.
**previous_notes**: Notes from May 10, 2024, indicated a PSA of 8.4 ng/mL following a rise from 19.4 ng/mL in March 2023, and advised continued urological follow-up for treatment planning. Notes from January 16, 2023, documented an initial PSA of 19.4 ng/mL and the recommendation for a biopsy to investigate rapid PSA velocity.
**family_history**: No family history was recorded.
**psa_trend**: The PSA trend shows values of 4.4 ng/mL in April 2022, 19.4 ng/mL in March 2023, 8.4 ng/mL in February 2024, and 86.0 ng/mL in January 2025.
**laboratory_results**: The most recent PSA is 86.0 ng/mL (as of January 21, 2025). Other labs include Free PSA at 17.70 ng/mL (21%), Haemoglobin at 16.2 g/dL, WBC at 6.4 x10^9/L, Platelets at 242 x10^9/L, Creatinine at 85 umol/L, eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73m2, Testosterone at 12.4 nmol/L, Alkaline phosphatase at 75 U/L, LDH at 206 U/L, and HbA1c at 5.8 %.

WHAT IS NOT RECORDED
The specific findings from the MRI that led to the PI-RADS 5 classification are detailed in the radiology report, but the clinical context surrounding the management decision is not fully synthesized. The final management decision remains pending.

WHAT THIS SUPPORTS
The data strongly supports a diagnosis of high-grade prostate cancer (Gleason 4+4, ISUP grade group 4/5) with local extension suggested by the PI-RADS 5 MRI finding and the palpable nodule on DRE. The rapid and significant progression of the PSA (from 4.4 to 86.0 ng/mL) indicates aggressive disease progression.
